name: Luang Prabang
tagline: Temples and slow mornings on the Mekong
summary: A small peninsula of gilded temples and French-era villas between two rivers. Wake early, swim at Kuang Si, and do very little in the hot afternoon.
seasonNote: March and April bring smoke from field burning; rain falls May to October.
arrival: The airport is 15 minutes from town; the Laos-China railway links Vientiane in about 2 hours.
gettingAround: Walk or cycle the peninsula; shared tuk-tuks and minivans run to the waterfalls.
cashTip: Mostly cash in kip; ATMs have low limits, so bring some US dollars or Thai baht as backup.
foodTip: Try khao soi Luang Prabang, laap, sticky rice with jeow bong chilli paste and Mekong river weed.
buyTip: Handwoven textiles from Ock Pop Tok and crafts at the night market.

connections.note: Seasonal direct flights; otherwise via Bangkok.

items.name: Kuang Si Falls
items.summary: A tiered waterfall with turquoise pools for swimming, plus a bear rescue centre at the entrance.
items.expect: Crowded from late morning; water turns brown in the rainy season.
items.tip: Arrive at opening and walk up to the main fall before swimming.

items.name: Morning alms giving
items.summary: At dawn, lines of monks in saffron robes walk the streets to receive sticky rice.
items.expect: A religious ritual, not a show; some tourists behave badly.
items.tip: Watch quietly from across the road, without flash, and keep your distance.

items.name: Pak Ou Caves by Mekong boat
items.summary: Two cliff caves filled with thousands of Buddha figures, reached by slow boat.
items.expect: The boat ride is the highlight; the caves are small.
items.tip: Take the morning boat and bring a torch for the upper cave.
